text:
Liam: quick sync - we keep seeing tenant complaints about inconsistent reads right after writes when clients hit a different region. we need a lightweight guarantee for read-after-write without full global sync.
Priya: agreed. current active-active assumes eventual consistency; some product flows expect immediate visibility for a short window (few seconds).
Jordi: two options: client sticky routing (mutate -> return session token with home-region hint) or optimistic local read with sync-check in background. both have tradeoffs.
Nina: sticky is simple but breaks load balance and complicates mobile clients that roam. optimistic local read means reads might miss, then we fetch remote and backfill - higher read latency tail.
Priya: what about a hybrid: return a short-lived 'write-hint' cookie/token that routes reads for that resource to the origin region for N seconds. fallback: proxy can use hint if present.
Liam: how do we prevent misuse? clients might flood a single region. we can scope hints per-resource and rate-limit per-tenant.
Jordi: and implement a server-side TTL: hint includes expire_ts and originating epoch; proxies enforce per-tenant concurrency caps.
Nina: legal: for EU-only tenants, the hint must not cause cross-border fetches. if origin is EU, fine; but origin in non-EU cannot be hinted to EU. we need policy table per-tenant.
Priya: agreed. tenant.policy residency enum {EU_ONLY, REGION_PREFERRED, GLOBAL}. hint handshake needs to check allowed_regions.
Liam: what about failover: if home region is down, reads with hint should auto-fallback to nearest allowed replica but mark result as degraded and emit a metric.
Jordi: metric + header X-Read-Consistency: origin|fallback|stale. helps signals for product teams.
Nina: implementation detail: where to store hint state? JWT-like compact token signed by control plane so proxies don't need a DB lookup. token payload: {tenant, resource_id, origin_region, exp, sig}. proxies validate signature.
Priya: good. signature key rotation must be easy. control plane distributes public keys to edge proxies via config.
Liam: how to handle multi-write races? two concurrent writes in different regions for same resource -> hints may conflict. need last-write-wins based on wall-clock? meh.
Jordi: better: include vector-clock-ish epoch number from write coordinator. each write increments tenant0epoch. hints carry epoch. on read, if local epoch < hint.epoch then proxy can attempt origin read or trigger quick sync.
Nina: where does epoch live? control plane shard per-tenant; small write-path cost but keeps ordering.
Priya: downside: extra RPC on writes to bump epoch. but writes are already indexed; we can piggyback epoch bump in write transaction.
Liam: performance thought: to avoid too many origin reads, proxies should consult a small LRU cache of recent write epochs per-resource. misses cause origin fetch.
Jordi: also consider a 'soft-stale' threshold: if hint age > 2s, allow local read and mark stale. reduces origin traffic.
Nina: testing: we need chaos tests that kill origin region and measure how quickly hints expire and how many stale reads happen.
infra-bot: note: add telemetry for hint_hit, hint_miss_origin_fetch, hint_fallback_used, epoch_mismatch_count.
Priya: security: token must not reveal PII. keep payload minimal and opaque if needed for strict tenants.
Liam: action items: Priya draft design doc with token format and policy table; Jordi prototype proxy token validator + caching; Nina run residency policy matrix and map tenants; infra-bot create ticket ENG-ARCH-770.
Jordi: aiming for prototype in 10 days.
Nina: I'll coordinate product on UX expectations for eventual stale reads (to show spinner/refresh).
Liam: ok - one more idea: for write-heavy streams we can offer 'sync write' API that guarantees local replication before 200 OK. expensive but opt-in.
Priya: include cost model for sync writes in doc.
Liam: great. wrap up: hybrid write-hint + epoch + smart proxy fallback seems promising. we'll discuss in next architecture sync.
